grades.reason: This is only a table of contents. It lists a Sleep and Wakeup chapter but says nothing about why a waiter might sleep forever after a wakeup.

grades.quote: This is a somewhat error-prone arrangement, because all concurrent waiters need to pass in the same mutex.
grades.reason: It names two possible causes of lost or ineffective wakeups. Concurrent waiters must all pass the same mutex to the wait call. Signaling without holding the mutex invites race bugs. It does not directly explain the lost-wakeup scenario.

grades.quote: There is no danger of waking too few threads. Either you have some way to know that only one is waiting, or you know that only one would be able to proceed, with the others looping back to waiting.
grades.reason: It explains how a wakeup can run and still leave a waiter asleep. Using notify instead of notifyAll can wake too few threads or the wrong thread, so the thread that could proceed keeps sleeping. This matches the symptom, though it is not framed as a general lost-wakeup diagnosis.

grades.quote: you need some mechanism that allows a thread to wait until circumstances are appropriate for it to proceed.
grades.reason: It is introductory background on why threads wait on condition variables. It does not address why a waiter would miss a wakeup or sleep forever.
